Then terminal gap<=0 yields printed sharp bound and Young bound. Repeating final hint instead requires adding h_(T+1)(u)-h_(T+1)(z), not cancelling it. The repeated-hint quadratic completion is refuted; no statement of equivalence to literal original is accepted.

mathematics: Each actual point minimizes the regularizer, current hint and strict past loss over V. The positive hinted curvature is in some genuine norm that can depend on the round.

For the additional terminal point, hold the final regularizer fixed. Setting the hint to zero gives a minimizer of the inclusive objective even at assigned curvature zero. Any such minimizer admits the sharp regret bound.

The Young bound uses the actual induced dual norm and requires all chosen curvatures strictly positive. Repeating the hint instead contributes its value at the comparator minus its value at the repeated-hint endpoint.
This is a labelled source repair. A feasible support need not support an arbitrary ambient extension. Neither uniqueness of the zero-curvature endpoint nor a zero-curvature Young bound is inferred.
